column2: The heading of the benefits section is printed «االفوائد», a typographical slip for «الفوائد» (“Benefits”).

On the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Give the fixed shares (farāʾiḍ) to those entitled to them; and whatever the fixed shares leave over goes to the nearest male relative.” Agreed upon (al-Bukhārī and Muslim).

Al-farāʾiḍ (“the fixed shares”): the portions set in the Book of Allah, namely one half, one quarter, one eighth, one third, two thirds and one sixth. Bi-ahlihā (“to those entitled to them”): those who are entitled to them. “And whatever the fixed shares leave over goes to the nearest man by lineage”: to the deceased whose estate is inherited.
Al-Jaʿbarī (may Allah have mercy on him) said concerning the agnatic heirs (ʿaṣabah), in a single verse:
Give precedence by class, then by closeness, / and after both, give precedence by strength [of kinship].
The printed text reads الجعبدي, evidently for الجعبري (al-Jaʿbarī), the author of this well-known verse on the order of agnatic heirs.
Those given precedence in inheritance are the holders of fixed shares.
What remains after the fixed shares goes to the agnatic heir, who is every male related [to the deceased] through a male, who inherits.
The nearest is given precedence, then the next nearest, in inheritance, whether among the holders of fixed shares or the agnatic heirs.
The agnatic heir receives nothing if the fixed shares take up [the estate], that is, if nothing remains after them.
The agnatic heir, if he is alone, takes the whole estate.

This hadith guides us to the fact that when someone dies and leaves wealth and heirs, the holders of fixed shares are given their shares in full—they are those who inherit by an amount set in the Book of Allah—and whatever wealth remains after the fixed shares
is the right of the nearest male relative of the deceased, who is the agnatic heir who inherits without a fixed amount.

This is from Allah's kindness, justice and mercy to His servants, in that He has given every heir a known, clear and evident right, to settle disputes and discord and prevent chaos from spreading through the strong overpowering the weak and the old the young,
in order to protect rights and secure for every holder of a right his right.
This cannot be accomplished except by knowing arithmetic, about which the poet says:
Were it not for arithmetic, by which every fixed share is known, / neither the unlawful nor the lawful would be known.
